messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int n = 0;
while (n < 4) { int hits = 0; hits++; n++; }

Question: What is hits in the last pass?
The student answered: 4

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The total keeps its value across passes even if it is set again inside the loop

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: long-winded, walks through the steps one by one, 20 to 35 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["I looked at n starting at zero and going up by one each time, so hits must also be counting up to four.", "Each pass hits becomes one more, so by the last pass when n is three it has grown to four.", "The line hits++ adds one every single loop, so after four passes the final value is four.", "Started with hits at zero, then it gets incremented each time until the loop ends, giving four.", "Since the loop runs four times and hits goes up by one each time, the last pass shows four."]}

sentences: I looked at n starting at zero and going up by one each time, so hits must also be counting up to four.
Each pass hits becomes one more, so by the last pass when n is three it has grown to four.
The line hits++ adds one every single loop, so after four passes the final value is four.
Started with hits at zero, then it gets incremented each time until the loop ends, giving four.
Since the loop runs four times and hits goes up by one each time, the last pass shows four.
